leftEvidence.role: The baptism becomes a public question
leftEvidence.title: Mark links Jesus’ authority question to John’s baptism

points.label: Event action and claim
points.left: Chief priests, scribes, and elders ask by what authority Jesus acts; he answers with a question about John’s baptism.
points.right: While Jesus teaches in the Temple, leaders demand the source of his authority; he asks about John’s baptism.

points.label: Response and consequence
points.left: They reason about heaven, unbelief, and fear of the crowd, then say they do not know.
points.right: They debate consequences, answer that they do not know, and receive no direct answer.

payload.posture: Both preserve heaven/human alternatives, fear of the people, and professed ignorance.

rightEvidence.role: The baptism becomes a public question
rightEvidence.title: Luke preserves the same authority deadlock

payload.tension: Luke locates the exchange while Jesus teaches and announces good news in the Temple.
payload.title: The authority deadlock in Mark and Luke
